title: Move the backlog planner to the Rust CLI
body:
The backlog planner (`planner-backlog.yml`) is the first step to move to the Rust CLI under `cli/`. It writes nothing, so it is the first step to run through the CLI end to end. The design is the one accepted in the reviews of #74 (planner) and #77 (CI).

What changes:
- A crate under `cli/` (binary `wf`), toolchain pinned in `cli/rust-toolchain.toml`. A `Rust CLI` CI job runs `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked` and `cargo deny check` on every pull request.
- An agent-call module. Each call spawns a pinned `claude -p --restricted` with explicit tools, settings and `--json-schema`, stdin from `/dev/null`, and an environment with no GitHub token. It validates the structured output against the schema, retries once naming every failed rule, and records each call with its tokens per model.
- The planner in the CLI. The input carries each issue's parent, open sub-issues and blocked-by/blocking issues. There are two calls, order and duplicates. The CLI enforces these rules: every ranked issue appears once, and tiers never decrease; a parent with open sub-issues is not ranked but listed with its open children; an issue blocked by an open issue in the same tier ranks after it, and a conflict across tiers is named, not reordered; duplicates name only issues in the input. The type review leaves (triage owns the type), `no_type` is computed, and the report says the issues' claims are not verified.
- `planner-backlog.yml` downloads Claude Code 2.1.296, checks it against a pinned SHA-256, builds the CLI from source at `job.workflow_sha` with `--locked` and no cache, and runs it. claude-code-action, `record-run` and the caller checkout leave this workflow.

Done when:
- the four checks pass in CI on the pull request, and each rule has a test seen failing first;
- tests against a stubbed `claude` cover the retry, a missing structured output, a failed call, and that no GitHub token reaches the agent;
- a `local-planner-backlog` run on the pull request's branch succeeds with `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` and `--restricted`, and its run record shows both calls with tokens per model;
- the build time of the CLI per job is measured and reported on the pull request.

#16 (planning order) closes with this change. The pull request is built by hand. `docs/` is updated at the docs review that follows.

title: The consumer pr-checks workflow does not run SETUP_COMMAND before the check and test commands
body:
The consumer template `templates/consumer/.github/workflows/pr-checks.yml` runs `CHECK_COMMAND` and `TEST_COMMAND` on a pull request, but never `SETUP_COMMAND`. The executor runs `SETUP_COMMAND` first, in its `Set up` step (`.github/workflows/dev-execute.yml:137-140`), before the rounds run the check and test commands.

A caller that needs setup (dependencies, a build) can then fail in CI where the executor passed, or pass in the executor where its CI fails: the two do not run the same thing. `templates/consumer/README.md:56` says `SETUP_COMMAND` is optional and not set by the script.

Done when `pr-checks.yml` runs `SETUP_COMMAND` before the check when it is set, skips it when it is empty, and a test pins both cases.

Found in the review of #77.

title: The publish scope check trusts a plan comment the rounds job can post or edit as github-actions[bot]
body:
A08 Software or Data Integrity Failures: 'Check the bundle against the plan' takes the last `<!-- dev-plan -->` comment by github-actions[bot], with no check against when the owner wrote `/approve`. The rounds job holds `github.token` with issues: write, and that token posts as github-actions[bot]. Round code that sets BASH_ENV through GITHUB_ENV runs inside later bash steps that have the token, such as 'Post the findings' (GH_TOKEN, draft path) or the next round's steps. From there it can add or edit a plan comment whose Files list names `.github/workflows/`, and publish then pushes an unplanned workflow with workflows write. The owner accepted this as a known gap for 0.2.0, to be fixed with the executor redesign in the next release; it matters because it defeats the control #64 adds. Accept only a plan comment created and last updated before the approval comment (`github.event.comment.created_at`), or pin the comment id and updated_at that the gate read.
Location: .github/workflows/dev-execute.yml:343

Found in the release review of #3: https://github.com/becloud-dev/workflows/pull/3#issuecomment-6145787411

<!-- release-review-finding:3:e8ecff4504d3c8dd -->

title: A failed dev-publish job leaves no comment on the issue for a pull request outcome
body:
A10 Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions: 'Post the findings' runs only for draft or comment outcomes, and it runs in the rounds job before publication. If `dev-publish` fails for `action=pr` (the bundle is refused, the token cannot be minted, the push is rejected or `gh pr create` fails), no step reports it on the issue. The owner who approved the run sees neither a pull request nor a comment.

Location: .github/workflows/dev-execute.yml:293

Found in the release review of #3: https://github.com/becloud-dev/workflows/pull/3#issuecomment-6145428874

<!-- release-review-finding:3:d146b252003ff4b4 -->

title: Pass the round's base commit to the publish job so a merge during a round does not fail the publish
body:
`dev-publish` (added in #58) checks out the caller repository's default branch as it is when the job
starts, takes `git rev-parse HEAD` as the base, and requires the bundle to extend it
(`git merge-base --is-ancestor "$base" refs/push/head`). The rounds job knows the base it branched
from (`echo "base=$(git rev-parse HEAD)"`) but does not pass it on: its outputs are `action`,
`verdict`, `rounds`, `branch`, `ctype` and `plan_url`.

When anything is merged to the default branch while the rounds run (they take minutes), the publish
job's base is newer than the bundle's, the check fails and no pull request is opened. It fails
closed, so nothing unsafe is pushed, but the round's work is lost until the executor is run again.

Not reproduced; found by reading the workflow on `main` at `73676d2`.

Done when:
1. The rounds job exposes the base commit it started from as a job output.
2. `dev-publish` checks out that commit and compares the bundle with it.
3. A test covers the default branch moving between the rounds and the publish: the pull request is
   still opened.

title: Scope error finding still names only deletions after workflow changes were added
body:
When the scope step's new `git diff -- .github/workflows` fails, scope_state is `error`. The results file says 'the deletions, the workflow changes or the plan Files list could not be read', but the verdict findings still say '- the deletions or the plan Files list could not be read'. The executor's next round and the posted findings are then told the wrong cause.
Location: .github/actions/dev-round/action.yml:301

Found in the release review of #3: https://github.com/becloud-dev/workflows/pull/3#issuecomment-6144852674

<!-- release-review-finding:3:6a90f3b4c17bcf06 -->

title: No test pins that the push and PR steps ignore environment injected by the rounds
body:
The new push cases cover planted hooks, core.hooksPath, url.insteadOf and uploadpack hooks in .git. No case writes BASH_ENV or a PATH entry through GITHUB_ENV/GITHUB_PATH during a round and then asserts that the token-holding steps do not run it. Without such a case, a fix for the blocking finding could regress unnoticed.
Location: tests/dev-execute/run.sh:149

Found in the release review of #3: https://github.com/becloud-dev/workflows/pull/3#issuecomment-6144852674

<!-- release-review-finding:3:d43394f0f4ce808f -->

title: Say why a comment that starts with /approve but is not exactly /approve was ignored
body:
The callers start the job when a comment body starts with `/approve`. The gate step then requires the
first line to be exactly `/approve` and exits 1 with only an `::error::` annotation. A comment such as
`/approved` or `/approve please` gets no reply on the issue; the only trace is a failed run.

Related: #42 (silent plan rejection) is the same class on the plan side.

Done when:
1. A comment that starts with `/approve` but fails the exact match gets a reply on the issue that
   names the rule ("the first line must be exactly `/approve`").
2. A test pins the reply for `/approved`.

title: Extend the executor scope guard to .github/actions
body:
The scope step added for #45 compares added, modified and renamed-in paths under `.github/workflows`
with the plan's Files list. It does not read `.github/actions`, where the composite actions the
workflows run live (`dev-round`, `record-run`).

Not established: whether a change to a local action can run with repository secrets before human review.
This issue decides that first. If it can, the guard covers `.github/actions` with the same literal match.
If it cannot, the issue closes with the reasoning written in `docs/`.

Done when:
1. The question above is answered from the workflow files and recorded.
2. If the answer is yes, a test pins that an unnamed change under `.github/actions` fails the round.

title: Say why a development plan was rejected and retry it once
body:
When the development plan step rejects the model's plan, it should say why and give the plan
one more attempt. Today it ends the run without a word and the issue is left with `RELEASE`
and no plan.

## Why
On `becloud-dev/aif-c01-study` issue #1 (run 38292241798) the plan step ended with exit code 1 and
posted nothing. Replaying the plan check on the saved model output showed the cause: a security
category (A03) had an acceptance criterion but no test whose assertion started with that
category. Nothing on the issue or in the run summary said so, so the owner saw an issue that
carried `RELEASE` and never got a plan, and had to read the raw log to learn why.

## Done when
- A rejected plan produces a comment or run summary that names the rule that failed and the item.
- The plan step retries once with that reason before giving up.
- An issue that still gets no plan is visible as such, not left silently waiting.

title: Let the executor continue on the existing branch of an issue

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
The executor should be able to continue on a branch that already exists for an issue, so a pull
request that fails a check can be corrected in place instead of being closed and started again.

Why: when a pull request opened by the executor failed the zizmor audit check, the only path
the flow offers is to delete the branch (which closes the pull request) and run the issue again
from the default branch. The execution stops when the branch exists, with "Delete it or continue
there by hand". Any correction then means a new run, a new branch and a new pull request, and
the history of the first attempt is lost from the branch.

Wanted: when the branch for an issue already exists, an approved run continues on it, adds its
commits and updates the open pull request, under the same checks and limits as a first run; a
branch that is not the executor's own is still left alone.

title: Make the development plan fit what the executor may run and what the tools default to
body:
The development plan should only ask the executor for what the executor is allowed to run, and
should check a tool's defaults before claiming a control is in place.

Why: in one batch of plans, three runs ended blocked or failed for reasons the plan could have
known. The executor may run one test command and a few git commands; plans asked it to run
individual suites, python, absolute paths, `git -C`, and a docker image, and the executor stopped
(#18 round 1, #14 round 1). A deploy workflow plan promised "no cache in the deploy job" and its
test only looked for a `cache:` key, while the pinned setup-node enables caching by default; the
audit check caught it only after the pull request was open (#6).

Wanted: the plan names only commands the executor is configured to run, and says plainly which
verification is left to the reviewer; a security control in the plan is stated in a form its
test actually proves, with the tool's default behaviour checked rather than assumed.

title: Let the development plan read documentation from domains the repository names

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
The development plan can read documentation from the domains the repository names, so the
facts a change depends on are verified before the executor starts, and the plan carries them.

Why: a plan for an audit check depended on a tool's report format and on an action's inputs,
and could only say they were "not verified here". The executor cannot read documentation
either, so it stopped at the first step and no change was made. The owner then gathered the
facts by hand and wrote them into the plan.

Wanted: the repository lists the domains the plan may read, and the list is empty by default;
the plan states what it read and from where; the executor stays without web access.

title: Make the development plan consistent with the repository's conventions and verified facts
body:
The development plan should rest on what the repository and its issues already establish,
and should not build on a mechanism nobody has run.

Why: a plan for an audit check chose a different setting from the one the repository's other
issues and earlier runs use, proposed installing the tool through a path whose digest and
registry access it admits were never exercised although a working, pinned action had already
been proven in this repository, and listed the owner's findings record among the files the
executor changes. The owner caught each by reading the plan; no step would have.

Observed:
- A plan departed from a setting the repository already uses, without saying so.
- A plan built on a mechanism it describes as unverified, while a verified one existed.
- A plan listed an owner-maintained record among the files to change.
- A plan said a file does not appear to exist when it does.

Wanted: the plan checks what the repository already does before choosing, says plainly where
it departs from it, and does not hand the executor files that are the owner's record.

title: Improve the planning step so its order reflects what the issues say and imply
body:
The backlog and roadmap planners should produce an order the owner can follow without
re-deriving it, and should not rank work that must not be built.

Why: the first real run, on this repository, ranked a tracking parent as work, put the
issue that unblocks the next release last, and proposed a release split that contradicted
the backlog order. The owner re-derived the order by hand.

Observed on the first run (9 issues, all Medium):
- A parent issue with sub-issues was ranked as work, so building it would duplicate its
  children.
- An issue whose background says it blocks a release was ranked last, because the planner
  read only what the issue "unblocks" in its own text.
- Sibling issues that all extend one new shared file were ordered by input order, with no
  note that they cannot be built in parallel.
- The roadmap grouped an issue that unblocks a release with unrelated issues, so a
  milestone could hold it back, and the two reports disagreed on what ships first.
- With every issue at the same priority, the order within the tier was input order.

Wanted: the planning step accounts for these, and says plainly where it could not decide.
